findings.fact: w2c_size measures ON_ConvertUTF16ToUTF8 with testByteOrder0/errorMask0/replacement0 and returns a nonnegative converted-prefix byte count after logging errors. w2c writes with errorMask0xffffffff/replacement0xfffd into that measured capacity; it cannot append replacement/suffix beyond a strict-prefix capacity.

on_wcsicmp uses current CRT if its parallel ASCII scan reaches a terminator in either string. If both current units remain nonzero at a non-ASCII stop, it converts both C prefixes to UTF8 and calls CompareStringA with stored locale1,flags0x20001,counts-1. Native results1/2/3 normalize to-1/0/1; other results fall back to current CRT.

ANSI MakeLower scans the wide C prefix before conversion. LCMapStringA uses locale1/flags0x100/sourceCount=n converted bytes/destinationCapacity=2*n+16. Failure or excessive result falls back to CRT on the original string; successful byte-string assignment replaces the old wide value, including loss of any original post-NUL stored suffix.

ON_wString assignment from ON_String obtains byteCount via strlen and uses CopyToArray/c2w. c2w calls ON_ConvertUTF8ToUTF16 with testByteOrder0/errorMask0xffffffff/replacement0xfffd and retains the actual returned wide length. Default .NET replacement grouping is not presumed equivalent to the legacy decoder.

The public NLS1 ANSI backend uses CP1256 on the recorded host, not system ACP1252. All65536 ANSI comparisons match corresponding CP1256-decoded CompareStringW controls;10460 differ from system-ACP decoded controls.
